title: The River Remembers Backwards
tagline: When the world forgets its rules, a woman must remember the songs that stitch reality together.
themes: Constraint as the Catalyst for True Freedom

chapters.title: The Fox with Too Many Tails
The Map That Was a Body
The Treaty of Flesh and Thread
The Animal with One Leg in Each World
The Constraint That Holds the World

story: Write a scene where a character discovers an everyday object (a spoon, a book, a coat) behaving according to its original, pre-colonial purpose or material truth, not its current use.
Create a dialogue between a surrealist painter and an Indigenous elder describing the same 'broken' phenomenon, one in artistic terms, the other in spiritual/cosmological terms.
Draft a 'legal document' from the perspective of the land itself, listing grievances and terms for a new treaty with humanity.
Imagine a 'Council of Broken Things'—a gathering of inanimate objects and natural features that have begun to malfunction. What do they debate? What is their plan?
technical: Build an interactive web experience where text flows in multiple directions (like the river), and the user must 'listen to the between sound' to navigate and reveal the story.

Create a generative art piece that uses a map as a seed. The program 'unpicks' the map based on user interaction, slowly transforming it from political boundaries into ecological or ancestral memory patterns.

cover_prompt: A woman stands in a flowing river, her hands weaving shimmering threads of light and memory from the water's surface, stitching a fractured sky back together as geometric patterns of imposed reality dissolve into organic, ancestral forms around her, [atmospheric setting with mood-condensed details: within a surreal river valley where clockwork gears rust into vines and city buildings melt into ancient, wise mountains, under a twilight sky where constellations rearrange into the faces of elders], in the atmospheric style of Remedios Varo and Leonora Carrington blended with the symbolic visual language of contemporary Indigenous surrealist artists like Jaune Quick-to-See Smith and Brian Jungen, [book cover framing, centered composition, dramatic low-angle shot looking up at the woman as she works, creating a sense of monumental scale and reverence], [dramatic chiaroscuro lighting with a color palette of deep indigo, river-silt brown, luminous silver thread-light, and eruptions of volcanic gold and moss green], masterpiece, best quality, ultra detailed, intricate details, professional composition, sharp focus, 8k resolution, flux dev.
